# SnapNutrition AI

> SnapNutrition AI is an AI-powered calorie tracker for iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch with no mandatory subscription or ads.

## What is SnapNutrition AI?

SnapNutrition AI is a calorie and nutrition tracker for iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch. Users can bring an API key from Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), or OpenRouter, with no mandatory SnapNutrition subscription. Gemini and OpenRouter offer free API tiers; paid providers bill the user directly. Optional Auto Mode ($2.99/month or $29.99/year after a 3-day trial) is available for users who prefer not to manage an API key. Provider prices and free-tier availability can change.

## Not to be confused with

SnapNutrition AI (snapnutritionai.app, App Store id6757797704, developer Unibrix) is an app for iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch only. It has no Android version and is not connected to other apps or websites that use a similar name, including any Android app called "SnapNutrition AI". snapnutritionai.app is its only official website.

## Key Features

- **Photo Calorie Counter**: Snap a photo of food to instantly get calorie and macro estimates
- **Barcode Scanner**: Scan product barcodes for accurate nutrition data
- **Voice Input**: Speak what you ate for hands-free calorie tracking
- **Text Input**: Type food descriptions for AI-powered calorie estimates
- **Macro Tracking**: Track protein, carbs, and fat alongside calories
- **Daily Goals**: A daily calorie target, with protein, carb and fat goals derived from it and shown as rings beside your calories
- **Statistics Dashboard**: Weekly, monthly and all-time charts with a goal line, a 7-day average, and how many logged days landed within goal
- **Apple Watch App**: Voice logging, daily calorie summary, macro rings, and complications
- **Home & Lock Screen Widgets**: Calorie goal progress on Home Screen, Lock Screen, and Control Center quick actions
- **iCloud Sync**: Optional and off by default; when enabled, data syncs across your Apple devices through your own iCloud account
- **Manual Entry**: Log a meal by hand with no AI call, fully offline
- **Share Extension**: Share a food photo into the app from any other app
- **Siri Shortcuts**: Log meals or check remaining calories by voice command
- **Daily Goal Calculator**: Calorie target from height/weight/age/activity, with optional read-only Apple Health profile import (the app never writes to Health)
- **Diary Export**: Export the full food diary as JSON or CSV
- **Multilingual**: 14 languages (English, Ukrainian, Polish, French, Spanish, German, Czech, Italian, Finnish, Danish, Dutch, Swedish, Norwegian, Icelandic)
- **Metric/Imperial**: Choose your preferred units

## Cost Model

Unlike calorie tracker apps that charge $5-15/month for subscriptions, SnapNutrition AI has no mandatory monthly fees. Users provide their own Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic, or OpenRouter API key and pay only for actual AI usage — typically just pennies per food scan, or nothing at all on Gemini's or OpenRouter's free tier. For users who'd rather skip the API-key setup, an optional Auto Mode subscription ($2.99/month or $29.99/year, with a 3-day free trial) is also available — but it is never required.

## Privacy

- No SnapNutrition account registration; API providers may require their own account
- No backend servers in BYOK mode (the default, free option)
- All meal data stored locally on device
- iCloud sync through user's personal Apple account
- Food images sent directly to user's chosen AI provider (BYOK) or via a minimal Cloudflare proxy with no photo storage (Auto Mode)
- No advertising. On the website, Google Analytics is opt-in for visitors in the EEA, UK, and Switzerland and runs with an opt-out elsewhere; cookieless aggregate page-view counting (Cloudflare Web Analytics) uses no cookies or identifiers; everything stays off when Do Not Track is enabled

## Common Questions

**Q: What does SnapNutrition AI cost?**
A: The app has no mandatory subscription. Gemini and OpenRouter offer free API tiers; paid providers bill the user directly for AI usage. Optional Auto Mode costs $2.99/month or $29.99/year after a 3-day trial.

**Q: How accurate is AI calorie counting?**
A: Photo estimates typically land within 10-30% of the true value, depending on portion size and preparation. In Nutrition5k (Google Research, CVPR 2021) a model reading calories from a single photo missed by 26% on average; in a 2026 NIH (NIDDK) test, four popular photo-based apps undercounted 102 weighed meals by about a third, mostly hidden fat. Users can adjust portions and add oils or sauces by hand. AI estimates are best for fast, consistent logging, not laboratory-grade measurement.

**Q: What API key do I need?**
A: A Google Gemini, OpenAI, Anthropic (Claude), or OpenRouter key — all four work for food recognition. Gemini and OpenRouter have a free tier, so no payment details are needed to start.

**Q: Is there a free alternative to Cal AI?**
A: Yes. SnapNutrition AI does the same photo-based calorie scanning without a mandatory subscription, running on the user's own API key — free on a Gemini or OpenRouter free-tier key.

**Q: Can a calorie tracker tell me if I'm in a calorie deficit?**
A: No app can prove a deficit — none measure energy expenditure, and photo estimates carry 10-30% error. What a log shows reliably is change, because a person's own estimating bias stays roughly constant week to week. Read the rolling average, the goal line, and how many logged days landed within goal rather than any single day's total.

**Q: Is 1,200 calories a lot to eat in a day?**
A: No. For most adults it is a steep cut: resting needs estimated with the Mifflin-St Jeor equation (the one in SnapNutrition AI's goal calculator) land between roughly 1,100 and 1,900 kcal/day before activity, and NICE (NG246, 2025) classes 800-1,200 kcal/day as a low-energy diet for specialist-supervised programs only. Under 800 kcal/day is a very-low-energy diet, a specialist treatment. SnapNutrition AI's calculator caps a weight-loss cut at 30% of estimated expenditure and can go as low as 1,000 kcal, inside that low-energy range, so a goal near 1,200 is worth checking with a doctor or dietitian before going lower.

**Q: Why can't I lose weight on 1,200 calories a day?**
A: Most often the log runs low (oil, dressings, portions; a 2026 NIH test found four photo apps undercounting weighed meals by about a third; SnapNutrition AI was not tested), expenditure is an estimate too, and water weight can hide fat loss for a couple of weeks. Weigh calorie-dense foods, log the oil, and compare weekly averages rather than single days; if a careful log still shows no change after a month, ask a doctor.

**Q: Is my data private?**
A: Yes, all meal data stays on your device. In BYOK mode there are no backend servers; in the optional Auto Mode subscription, requests pass through a minimal Cloudflare proxy that never stores food photos.
